args.text:
Batch: 25 runs. 15 accepted, 9 declined (r01, r03, r04, r06, r09, r10, r16, r20, r24), 1 not reported (r23).
Flagged: none.
Cleared (15): r02, r05, r07, r08, r11, r12, r13, r14, r15, r17, r18, r19, r21, r22, r25. Every check that was run passed on all of them.
- r02, r05, r11, r12, r25: the centre REGR peak is about 84 %/h, against a batch median of 42.4 %/h. Their peak position (316 µm) and growth-zone length (537–547 µm) match the batch, so their strain-rate profiles have the normal shape and these are read as faster roots. r02 and r05 kept frame-stride remedies (6→3→1). A stride change sets which frames are paired, not the frame-time base, so it does not change the rate. Full records were opened only for r02 and r05. r11, r12 and r25 were cleared from the batch table, which shows the same pattern of 2 remedies kept and no roll-backs.
- r08, r14, r17, r18, r21 used the width-free ratio, so plane sections was not run on them. Its value above the threshold there reflects a change in root width, not a failure. The width-free ratios of r17 (−0.472) and r18 (−0.421) have |z| ≥ 3.2. That comes from a batch MAD of 0.005, and each differs from the median (−0.445) by only about 6 %.
In common among flagged runs: none. Among the declined runs, the ones far from the batch failed rigid-body invariance, which means the tracker failed. The rest had a profile like the batch but failed closure and plane sections.
